trial_title: Dutch Intracerebral Hemorrhage Surgery Trial Pilot Study
brief_summary:
Background:

Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) accounts for 15-20% of all strokes in Western Europe, and contributes profoundly to mortality and disability. Thirty day case fatality is 40% and of those surviving, only few gain independence. Except for stroke unit care and early blood pressure lowering there is currently no treatment of proven benefit. eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score of ≥2?

eligibility_table.criterion: Supratentorial ICH confirmed by CT, without a CT-angiography confirmed causative vascular lesion (e.g. aneurysma, arteriovenous malformation [AVM], dural arteriovenous fistula [DAVF], cerebral venous sinus thrombosis [CVST]).
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has an arteriovenous malformation (AVM), which is a causative vascular lesion, thus not meeting the inclusion criterion.
No lab values in patient profile
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient's intracerebral hemorrhage lesion volume measure at least 10 mL?

eligibility_table.criterion: Intervention can be started within 8 hours from symptoms onset; or for controls presentation within 8 hours of symptom onset.
eligibility_table.justification: The information does not specify the exact time of symptom onset relative to intervention availability.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Did the patient present to the hospital within 8 hours of symptom onset?

eligibility_table.criterion: Patient's or legal representative's written informed consent
eligibility_table.justification: Assuming the patient or legal representative can provide informed consent, this criterion is likely met.

eligibility_table.criterion: Pre-stroke disability, which interferes with the assessment of functional outcome at 90 days, i.e. mRS > 2
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has a significant medical history that may affect functional outcomes, but specific mRS score is not provided.

eligibility_table.criterion: Causative vascular lesion (e.g. aneurysm, AVM, DAVF, CVST) on CT-angiography or other known underlying cause (e.g. tumor, cavernoma)
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has a known AVM, which is a causative vascular lesion, thus this criterion is met.

eligibility_table.criterion: Untreated coagulation abnormalities, including INR > 1.3 (point of care measurement allowed) and treatment with oral thrombin or factor X antagonists; patients on vitamin K antagonist can be included after correction of the INR.
eligibility_table.justification: No lab values provided to assess coagulation status; cannot determine if this criterion is met.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Is the patient's INR greater than 1.3 based on the most recent point of care measurement?

eligibility_table.criterion: Current known severe infection for which antibiotic treatment at time of ICH symptom onset
eligibility_table.justification: No information provided regarding current infections; cannot determine if this criterion is met.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a current known severe infection that requires antibiotic treatment at the time of ICH symptom onset?

eligibility_table.criterion: Patient moribund (e.g. coning, bilateral dilated unresponsive pupils)
eligibility_table.justification: No information provided regarding the patient's current state of health; cannot determine if this criterion is met.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient exhibit bilateral dilated unresponsive pupils with a Glasgow Coma Scale score of ≤8?

eligibility_table.criterion: Pregnancy (note: most patients will be beyond child bearing age; if not a pregnancy test is mandatory).
eligibility_table.justification: No information provided regarding pregnancy status; cannot determine if this criterion is met.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient undergone a pregnancy test within the last 48 hours?
